subject: Re: Pilot credits extension & burn-rate check
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Priya Rao <priya@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-25T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot credits & next steps — Acme initial recap

Alex / Priya,

Great to meet earlier — thanks for the time. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery: 

- What we heard: Acme is evaluating Redwood to power in-app summarization and search. Primary constraints are cost predictability and inference latency for short responses.
- Current production-ish traffic: ~25M tokens/month across teams (some variance).
- Pilot plan: ramp to ~3M tokens/week across 2 routes (summaries + faqs) — projected pilot burn ~12M tokens/month.
- Budget check: Acme is targeting roughly $300–$400 per 1M tokens (target $/1M tokens) for the pilot to be defensible against current vendor spend.
- Primary success criteria: latency < 500ms p50 for summaries, predictable monthly cost within the budget band, and integration of fallback routing.

Next steps (owners):
1) Marissa (me) — send usage template and confirm pilot extension/credits ask (today).
2) Alex/Priya — share historical token burn and budget owner contact (by EOD Wed).
3) Vivek — offer quick infra checklist and model variant recommendations for cost savings (this week).

Two asks on our side:
- Could you share a 30-day usage export so we can calibrate batching/quantization recommendations? (attachment is fine)
- If pilot burn looks like ~12M/month, would you be open to a 60-day credits extension while we validate unit economics? That helps us demonstrate TCO benefits.

I can draft a short credits extension (no-cost) for leadership approval — want to confirm target amount. Based on the numbers above, a conservative extension to cover 50–60k extra requests (~50k–80k tokens per request varies) should get you through the validation window.

I'll follow up with a formal ask once you confirm the burn and the internal budget owner.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0132

Attachments: acme_usage_report.csv (requested)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>

Cc: Priya Rao <priya@acme.com>
Date: 2026-08-26T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot credits & next steps — Acme initial recap

Marissa — thanks for the summary. Confirming a few items from our side: 

- We pulled a 30-day export (attached) — current production ~22–28M tokens/month, pilot traffic expected to peak at ~14M tokens/month during accelerated testing.
- Budget owner (Priya) is comfortable with a pilot spend target of $350/1M tokens (ballpark) but needs a demonstration of unit-cost wins before committing to a higher monthly run-rate.
- We'd like to request a 60-day extension on the pilot credits and ~50,000 tokens of extra credits to cover the aggressive ramp. Can you confirm what that maps to in your credits accounting (how you show credits vs tokens)?

Also, two quick questions:
1) Can your team recommend a model/quantization profile that targets <$350/1M tokens while keeping our latency targets?
2) Is there a straight-forward way to track spend per-route in your console?

Thanks,
Alex
Head of Product — Acme Inc.
alex.johnson@acme.com\

Quick internal note after reviewing Alex's numbers and the pilot ask:
- Pilot peak of ~14M tokens/month is reasonable to support with an initial 60-day extension.
- Unit-economics: if Acme targets $350/1M tokens, we should push a model+quantization combo that delivers ~30–40% cost reduction over the default hosted model for the same quality bar. Vivek can validate two candidate model variants and provide a cost/latency table.

Proposal for credits: approve a 50,000-token credit pool for the pilot extension (this equates to the free credit bucket tied to the ACME-2026-P1 pilot). Need formal sign-off from Neha on the cap and expiration.

Marissa — if you can confirm the ask in a short email to Alex, I can attach an approval stub for signatures.
